result:
I'd make understanding cheaper than certainty.

Most of the damage people do to each other doesn't come from pure malice. It comes from the feeling that you already know what the other person is, what they want, and why they're wrong—and that pausing to actually find out would cost too much. Status, time, identity, the pleasure of being right. So the shortcut wins, and then the shortcut hardens into a world.

If understanding were the path of least resistance—if it felt easier, safer, and more rewarding to see someone clearly than to flatten them—a lot of cruelty, waste, and self-defeat would lose its fuel without anyone having to become a saint. Not perfect empathy. Just enough friction removed from looking again.
